clue.text: Under time pressure, revised kitchen catalogs

indicators.note: something revised has been reworked, so the letters of the last two words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone races to finish revising catalogues of kitchen goods before a deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges the fifteen letters of KITCHEN CATALOGS into the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Working against a deadline, with minutes ticking away, is an idiom for being hurried by limited time.

clue.text: 11 in a group of musicians in performance

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
a show that is on is being performed

explanation.surface: A member of a touring group of musicians is in mid-performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 11 across, DISOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up or forsake someone completely is to renounce them, a synonym of disown.

clue.text: Collect incorporated in 'a church service

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic Eucharistic church service

explanation.surface: A collection is taken during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collect' looks like the short prayer said at a service, but here it is a verb; 'incorporated in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather things together into a heap is to collect them, a synonym.

clue.text: Part of plane — whole seen to be damaged

indicators.note: damaged letters are knocked out of shape, so whole and seen are rearranged

explanation.surface: An inspector finds an aircraft component entirely damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be damaged' rearranges WHOLE SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The landing-gear wheel under an aircraft's front is a component of the plane.

clue.text: End of story, as the saying goes

indicators.note: the phrase points to how a word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Someone reaches the end of a story, quoting a proverb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as the saying goes' signals a soundalike: TALE, a story, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear or last part of something is its end, as with an animal's hindmost appendage.

clue.text: Man upset the second time in fear sounded like an ass

parts.note: HE is a man, the male pronoun

indicators.note: upset means turned over, and only the second copy of the man is turned

parts.note: the same man supplies a second HE
awed means filled with fear or dread

explanation.surface: A man, frightened a second time, brayed like a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset the second time' turns the second HE into EH; HE + EH + AWED.
explanation.definitionFit: The bray of a donkey is written as a two-syllable noise, so making it is braying like an ass.

clue.text: Drink up, Dad, before it gets cold

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
taken as written
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: Dad is told to drink up his tea before it goes cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before it gets cold' reads as the drink and dad preceded by the cold letter; the surface is a parent hurrying a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup of tea is called by this informal British word, so it is a drink.

clue.text: During Thursday, English revolutionary is busy

parts.note: on can mean during, as in on Thursday
a Trot is a Trotskyist, a revolutionary

explanation.surface: An English revolutionary is kept busy throughout Thursday.
explanation.walkthrough: In British idiom, being on the go all day without a break is being busy.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means continuously on the go, hence busy and active without rest.

clue.text: Relations call up in connection with motion

parts.note: kin are one's relations

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: to cite is to call or summon someone to court

explanation.surface: Relatives phone one another about a motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CITE into ETIC in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to or produced by movement, as in the energy of moving bodies.

clue.text: Water from an embankment given to farm animals

parts.note: a dam is an embankment holding back water
swine are pigs, farm animals

explanation.surface: Water from a reservoir wall is given to the livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an old humorous name for water, the only drink of the first man.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorous old name for plain drinking water, the only beverage Eden's first man had.

clue.text: Spike with broken point

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters of point are reassembled

explanation.surface: A spike has had its point snapped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges POINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A climber's metal peg driven into rock is a spike.

clue.text: Deny broadcast's drowned by distracting noise

indicators.note: being drowned by something means being swallowed up inside it

parts.note: din is loud distracting noise
to sow seed is to broadcast it, and the 's reads as is

explanation.surface: Someone denies that a broadcast was drowned out by noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests radio, but here it means scattering seed by hand; 'drowned by' signals one word swallowed inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuse to acknowledge or to repudiate someone is to deny them.

clue.text: Exotic bird puts a libertine in a' temper

indicators.note: the libertine is placed in the temper word

parts.note: a pet is a fit of temper, as in being in a pet
a rake is a libertine

explanation.surface: An exotic bird makes a womaniser lose his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe after the second 'a' is print noise; 'in a pet' is an old phrase for being in a sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brightly coloured parrot is a tropical, exotic bird.

clue.text: Seasoning from stone container put back

indicators.note: putting back means the joined words are written in reverse

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone
a tun is a large cask, a container

explanation.surface: Seasoning from a stone jar is replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns GEMTUN around.
explanation.definitionFit: The ground seed of an East Indian tree is a spice used as seasoning.

clue.text: Head girl team-leader was informed about

parts.note: the leading letter of team is T

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the informed word goes round the girl

parts.note: to have heard about something is to have been informed
Liz is a girl's name

explanation.surface: The head girl and the captain were told about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' is a headland: the most southerly point of mainland Britain, in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A head is a promontory, and this Cornish point is a famous headland.

clue.text: This connects me with various crimes -how fascinating!

indicators.note: various suggests a mixed assortment, so the letters of crimes are rearranged

explanation.surface: A detective links himself to a range of crimes, intrigued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' signals the rearrangement; the opening 'This connects' and 'how' are surface padding round an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hypnotic holds attention completely, which is to be fascinating.

clue.text: Play as alternative to Cats?

explanation.surface: A theatre fan suggests a different show instead of the musical.
explanation.walkthrough: Agatha Christie's long-running London play; also a device to catch mice instead of keeping cats. Cats is also a musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Christie's long-running thriller is a play, and a spring device for mice replaces a cat.

clue.text: Save articles in soft fabric

parts.note: bar and save both mean except
the articles A, THE and A

explanation.surface: Someone saves articles of soft cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' means except, not rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine woollen cloth used for suits and uniforms is a soft fabric.

clue.text: Deliver cargo of sponge

parts.note: to deliver someone is to set them free
a load is a cargo

explanation.surface: A courier delivers a cargo of sponges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sponge' is a verb: to live off others.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrounge off others without paying is to sponge.

clue.text: Military equipment company receives attention

indicators.note: receiving means taking another word inside

parts.note: a firm is a company
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: An arms supplier gets noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receives' signals one word taken inside another; 'company' is a business here, not companionship.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle or pistol is a weapon, part of military equipment.

clue.text: Piano, say, used in club

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A piano is played at a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' is a golf club used on the green.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat-faced stick used on the green is a golf club.

clue.text: Lessened — cut by about 50

parts.note: re means about or concerning
L is the Roman numeral fifty
axed means cut

explanation.surface: Something was reduced, cut by roughly fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut by about 50' places the cutting word after the about and fifty pieces, which come first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slackened, as a grip or tension, is lessened.

clue.text: Track made by dragoon

explanation.surface: A path was made by a cavalryman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dragoon' is a verb: to coerce someone; 'made by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A US railway line is a track, and to force someone into acting is to dragoon them.

clue.text: Put in actual name of an organ

indicators.note: one letter is put in the other word

parts.note: real means actual

explanation.surface: Someone inserts the real name of a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' is the kidney, not an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the kidneys, which are organs.

clue.text: Medical book written in smoother ballpoint

indicators.note: the letters are contained in the run of the words smoother ballpoint

explanation.surface: A medical text was written with a smooth ballpoint pen.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'smootHER BALLpoint'.
explanation.definitionFit: Old books listing plants and their healing uses served as medical guides.

clue.text: Distinguishing mark, of tailless nocturnal creature

indicators.note: the creature loses its tail, the final letter

parts.note: a badger is a nocturnal creature

explanation.surface: A distinguishing mark on a tailless night animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' drops the R from BADGER.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem worn to show membership or rank is a distinguishing mark.

clue.text: Ultimately this might uglify eye

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each word in turn

explanation.surface: An inflamed swelling might eventually spoil the look of someone's eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letters of the four words spell it, and the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed swelling on the eyelid can make an eye look unsightly.

clue.text: Military commander's home once more

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish military commander; the 's reads as is
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A general's house is visited a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: AGA is a Turkish officer's title; IN means at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something a second time is doing it once more.

clue.text: Dissident exhorted to change and accept love

indicators.note: accepting means taking in another letter
change means alter, so the letters of exhorted are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A dissenter was urged to reform and embrace love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges EXHORTED; 'accept' takes O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding views against established doctrine makes one unorthodox, a dissident.

clue.text: Expansion of corporation in historical period quietly studied

parts.note: the Middle Ages are a historical period
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: A firm's growth during a medieval era was quietly researched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is an old British jokey word for a paunch, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is a jocular term for a pot belly, so its expansion is the waistline gained around fifty.
